# Econ 588 current work

Week 2 is built and awaits John's first feedback. Refine this same slice until explicit close, then continue the next week. Preserve Week 1 and all prior course commitments; do not reopen old ideation-seat waits.

<details>
<summary>Established course plan and source spine</summary>

# PLAN — Econ 588 Student Summaries (CONFIRMED by John 2026-09-05)

John's amendments at confirmation: each week gets a **research pass** (researchPrime, with a
literature-review flavour: find the classic examples, datasets and supplementary readings that go
with the text) and an **ideation pass** (Jumper: how to illustrate the week's principle, which
examples land). Both feed the week's pack before it is reviewed.

**Standing rules (John, 2026-09-06).** (1) **Elegance, and no rabbit holes.** Every commissioned run is capped, runs the Rabbit-Catcher check at each boundary, parks what the goal does not need, and names what it cut. (2) **External sources are adversarially verified** before they enter a pack: any dataset, reading, video or example brought in from outside Greene and the study guide passes a fetched-and-checked review (researchPrime's adversarial round at medium stakes or a Gandalf read) and carries its evidence grade; nothing unverified is cited to a student. (3) **A refinement loop with John is part of every plan** (John, 2026-09-06): for every major deliverable, get a complete good version first, then iterate with him in as many rounds as it takes, and journal each round - what changed, why, and what it teaches the steward - so later efforts start better.

## Goal

Produce, one week at a time, a study pack for each week of Econ 588 that a strong-math,
stats-light first-year master's student can absorb fast: what to memorize, the big picture,
the intuition and the economics behind it, simple worked examples with clean graphics, and
runnable Python and R code that tie out to the same numbers — with an interactive Shiny
illustration for the principle of the week.

**Student assumed:** good mathematics (linear algebra, calculus, some probability), little formal
statistics or economics, good intuition. Nothing beyond that is presumed anywhere.

**Sources:** the Frandsen BYU study guide (the topic spine), Greene *Econometric Analysis* 8th
edition (chapters 1–4 in hand as text; the eText John is buying for the rest), the 5th-edition
scan for spot-checks, and Greene's public datasets.

## Observable success

- A student with the assumed profile reads one week's pack in an evening and can state the
  week's formulas, terms and ideas from the memorize sheet without the text.
- Every number in every pack is produced by BOTH a Python script and an R script, and a runner
  proves they agree to 1e-8 (or the pack is not released).
- Each week has at least one interactive Shiny illustration John has driven himself.
- Every claim ties to a Greene chapter/section and a study-guide section.

## The deliverable and its stable components (one pack per week)

| Component | What it is |
|---|---|
| Overview | One page: what this week is about, where it sits in the course, why an economist cares |
| Main points and flashcards | The week's scope in one line, the points to understand, then a flashcard deck (concepts, terms, formulas) as a clickable page and a printable list; sources go at the bottom of the page, never the top (John, round 1) |
| Intuition and economics | Where each idea comes from, the plain-language reason, the economic question it answers |
| Worked examples | Small simple datasets, step-by-step, with clean figures |
| Code | `python/` and `R/` scripts producing the same numbers and figures; a tie-out runner compares them. Reader-facing: an executable Python notebook and an R walkthrough, rendered with outputs to web pages the reader clicks through (John, round 1) |
| Interactive illustration | An R Shiny app with a few sliders for the principle of the week, reachable from a clickable launcher and a live link (plus static PNGs for the doc) |
| Self-check | A handful of questions with worked answers |

All weeks are chapters of ONE integrated report (`reports/ECON588-STUDENT-SUMMARIES-REPORT.md`
plus an embedded-resources HTML and a PDF), which opens with the **course overview** (John,
2026-09-07: a new deliverable, `COURSE-OVERVIEW.md/.html/.pdf`, which follows the BYU syllabus —
the Frandsen study guide — section by section in its order, with our week map as a column).
Each finished week is also packaged as a **student zip** (`deliverables/ECON588-Week<N>-student-pack.zip`):
one folder holding exactly the week's eight register items — page PDF, flashcard deck (HTML), Jupyter notebook
(.ipynb, outputs in place), R Markdown (.Rmd plus its knitted HTML), the Python and R scripts, the tie-out report,
the content review PDF — plus a README (what each file is, how to run the notebook, the R Markdown and the
scripts) and `data/`. The notebook, the R Markdown and the tie-out are executed inside the staged folder before it
is zipped (John, 2026-09-07: the register's week block and the zip are one list).

## Week map (proposal — week boundaries are John's to move)

| Wk | Topic | Study guide | Greene 8e (5e) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The econometric process and the linear model: question → model → data → estimation → inference; OLS as a minimization, normal equations, fitted values, residuals, R² | §1–2.5 | Ch 1–3 (1–3) |
| 2 | When OLS is right: the identifying assumption and how it fails (omitted variables, measurement error, simultaneity); unbiasedness, variance, Gauss–Markov; saturated regressions; Frisch–Waugh. Worked example: Greene's Monet cross-section (Table F4.1), moved here by John 2026-09-06 | §2.6–2.7 | Ch 3–4 (3–4) |
| 3 | Inference: consistency, the CLT, asymptotic normality, robust (White) standard errors, t and Wald tests, confidence intervals | §2.8 | Ch 4–5, App. D (5–6) |
| 4 | Generalized least squares: heteroskedasticity, serial correlation, SURE | family tree | Ch 9–10 (10–12, 14) |
| 5 | Generalized method of moments: moment conditions from theory (Euler equation), identification, weighting, overidentification test | §3 | Ch 13 (18) |
| 6 | Instrumental variables: why OLS fails, exclusion and rank conditions, 2SLS, optimal IV, specification tests, classic examples | §4–4.2 | Ch 8 (5, 15) |
| 7 | Simultaneous equations and panel data: reduced form, fixed effects, first differences, random effects, difference in differences | §4.3 + tree | Ch 6.4, 10–11 (13, 15) |
| 8 | Extremum estimators and maximum likelihood: M-estimators, consistency conditions, the sandwich, MLE as the leading case | §5, §6 intro | Ch 12, 14 (16–17) |
| 9 | Binary outcomes: probit and logit, marginal effects | §6.1 | Ch 17 (21) |
| 10 | Censoring and selection: Tobit and Heckit | §6.2–6.3 | Ch 19 (22) |
| 11 | Quantile regression and the delta method | §7–8 | Ch 7.3, App. D (16) |
| 12 | Nonparametric estimation: kernel density, kernel and local-polynomial regression, series and splines, regression discontinuity | §9 | Ch 7.4–7.5, 12.4 (16) |
| 13 | Treatment effects | §10 | Ch 8.5, 19.6 (22) |

## Roadmap (tagged; the cockpit shows these as the work product)

| Step | Part | Done when | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source spine and edition crosswalk | research | The week map above is confirmed, with study-guide sections and Greene 8e/5e chapter-section references per week, saved as `SPINE.md` | — |
| Toolchain and tie-out harness | slice | statsmodels and the R packages install; the tie-out runner executes both scripts for a week and fails on any mismatch beyond 1e-8 | `python tools/tieout.py --week 1` |
| Week 1 research pass | research | researchPrime report: the best worked examples, datasets and supplementary readings for the econometric process and the linear model, matched to Greene Ch 1–3 and guide §1–2.5 | — |
| Week 1 ideation pass | research | Jumper report: ranked ideas for illustrating OLS and the econometric process (figures, the Shiny sliders, the examples that land for a stats-light reader) | — |
| Week 1 pack | slice | All seven components exist for Week 1, informed by the research and ideation passes, and the tie-out passes | tie-out |
| Week 1 refinement loop with John | slice | John has read the pack and driven the explorer; his feedback is folded back in as many rounds as it takes until he calls it good; each round journaled | — |
| Week 1 review | rigor | Tie-out green, expert-coder review of both scripts, content review against Greene and the guide with the elegance filter, every external source adversarially verified with its evidence grade recorded, fixes applied | tie-out + review |
| Integrated report and register | integrate | Week 1 is a chapter of the report with figures embedded; DELIVERABLES and README point at it | — |
| Weeks 2–13 | harden | Each week repeats research → ideation → pack → review → refinement loop with John → integrate; each week becomes its own step when it starts | tie-out per week |

## What was cut (said aloud)

- ~~Jupyter notebooks~~ — reinstated by John in Week 1 round 1: notebooks are the reader's surface; the scripts remain the gate's.
- **Bayesian and time-series weeks** — not in the study guide; parked, not planned.
- **Week 2 research items parked (2026-09-07):** Greene's gasoline Example 4.2 (the price slope flips sign when income enters; reproduces to every printed digit), the Monet subsampling rows of Table 4.3 (Example A's experiment on real data), Longley (multicollinearity, a Week 2 preview only) and Example 3.1's partial correlations (Week 3 flags). Each is a good ten minutes; none is needed by the week's seven points. Folded instead: the omitted-variable identity on real data (Monet with SIGNED left out; Week 1's two school regressions) and the three free readings, flagged where they run ahead to Week 3.
- **OCR of the 5th-edition scan** — page images are read visually when a spot-check is needed; a text layer is not worth the tooling.
- **Hunting for an unauthorized 8th-edition PDF** — declined; the purchased eText drops in when it arrives.

</details>
